newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close sharply higher at 6-year peak.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close sharply higher at 6-year peak.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply up on Saturday as liquidity-driven buying across all sectors drove the index to a six-year high, brokers said.

The weighted index closed 99.42 points or 1.33 percent higher at 7,598.93. That surpassed the 7,536.28 close on Thursday, and was the market's highest finish since it ended at 7,857.01 on June 2, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$111.44 billion in Saturday's shortened session.
Taiwan's red hot market, buoyed by expectations of an economic recovery, has finished higher in nine of the last 10 sessions and gained more than 400 points over that span.

"Buying interest is still very strong despite the high index, which indicates that investors really want to push this bull run as far as they can," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
The heavily weighted financials topped all gains, rising 2.07 percent with China Development Corp closing T$6.50 higher at T$106.50.
Delta Electronics gained T$5.50 to T$102.50 on news that it signed a T$1.3 billion contract with Japanese battery giant Yuasa Corp to form a joint venture battery plant in Taiwan.
Brokers expected the market's momentum to slow somewhat on Monday. But the index likely would not suffer heavy profit-taking, they said.
